candidats.description: Cherokee Mixed-Use Lofts is an urban infill, mixed-use, market-rate housing project. The building is inspired by the series of paintings by the British artist Patrick Hughes titled, “Prospectivity”, whose paintings appear to be ever changing and physically moving while being viewed. At Cherokee the main architectural feature of this project is the building’s owner-controlled operable double façade system. candidats.description: Built in 1979, this contemporary mixed-use building was renovated in the early 2010s to its present appearance. The building features a facade clad in brick, glass curtain walls, and multi-colored metal panels, with wire mesh railings on the upper floors, and a recessed storefront at the retail spaces on the ground floor.

candidats.titre: File:Urban Lab Building (Morgan Live + Work), Morgan Street and 32nd Street, Bridgeport, Chicago, IL (54835393789).jpg
candidats.description: Built in 2002-2004, this Contemporary building was designed by Martin Felsen and Sarah Dunn to serve as their personal residence, as well as the home of their architecture and design firm, Urban Lab. The building consists of a one-story front wing, containing an architecture studio, with a principal facade clad in rusted cor-ten steel panels with perforated metal screens at the windows, corrugated metal panels on the side and rear facades, and a second-story wing that cantilevers onto a grassy mound in the rear, which is clad in metal panels with large bays and exposed steel cross-bracing.
